questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are $50°$ and $60°$. Find the third angle.
questions.explanation: The three angles of a triangle add to $180°$, so the third angle is $180° - (50° + 60°) = 180° - 110° = 70°$.

distractorRationale.b: Gave the sum of the two known angles instead of the remaining angle
distractorRationale.c: Subtracted from 190 by arithmetic slip
distractorRationale.d: Subtracted from 360°, which is the angle sum of a quadrilateral

questions.stem: What is the size of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: All three sides are equal, so all three angles are equal. Since they must total $180°$, each one is $180° \div 3 = 60°$.

distractorRationale.a: This is each acute angle of a right-angled isosceles triangle
distractorRationale.c: An equilateral triangle has no right angle
distractorRationale.d: This is the interior angle of a regular hexagon

questions.stem: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is $40°$. Find the size of each base angle.
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal. Subtracting the vertex angle leaves $180° - 40° = 140°$ to share between them, so each base angle is $140° \div 2 = 70°$.

distractorRationale.a: Halved the vertex angle instead of the remaining 140°
distractorRationale.b: Assumed all three angles are equal, which only happens in an equilateral triangle
distractorRationale.d: Gave the combined total of the two base angles

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has the two shorter sides 5 cm and 12 cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras' theorem the hypotenuse $c$ satisfies $c^2 = 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169$, so $c = 13$ cm. The 5, 12, 13 triple is worth memorising.

distractorRationale.a: Subtracted the two sides instead of using their squares
distractorRationale.c: Added the two sides directly, which always overestimates the hypotenuse
distractorRationale.d: Multiplied the two sides, which gives twice the area, not a length

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is 25 cm and one of the shorter sides is 7 cm. Find the length of the third side in centimetres. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Because the unknown is a shorter side, you subtract: $x^2 = 25^2 - 7^2 = 625 - 49 = 576$, so $x = 24$ cm. Adding the squares here would wrongly give a side longer than the hypotenuse.

questions.stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon.
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, and the interior angle sum is $(n - 2) \times 180° = (6 - 2) \times 180° = 720°$. The hexagon splits into four triangles from one vertex.

distractorRationale.a: Used $n = 5$, the pentagon
distractorRationale.c: Used $n = 7$, the heptagon
distractorRationale.d: Used $n = 8$, the octagon

questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $24°$. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon add to $360°$, and in a regular polygon they are all equal. So $n = 360 \div 24 = 15$ sides.

distractorRationale.a: Divided 360 by 30 rather than 24
distractorRationale.c: Divided 360 by 20
distractorRationale.d: Repeated the given angle as the number of sides

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is $150°$. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: Convert to the exterior angle first: $180° - 150° = 30°$. Then $n = 360 \div 30 = 12$ sides. Going straight to $360 \div 150$ would be meaningless.

distractorRationale.a: Divided 150 by 15, mixing up the two formulas
distractorRationale.c: Used an exterior angle of 24° instead of 30°
distractorRationale.d: Gave the exterior angle rather than the number of sides

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, the exterior angle at $C$ is $110°$ and angle $A$ is $40°$. Find angle $B$.
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so $110° = 40° + B$, giving $B = 70°$. Checking, the interior angle at $C$ is $70°$, and $40 + 70 + 70 = 180°$.

distractorRationale.a: Subtracted 40 from the interior angle at C rather than from the exterior angle
distractorRationale.c: Repeated the exterior angle
distractorRationale.d: Added 110 and 40 instead of subtracting

questions.stem: A ladder 10 m long leans against a vertical wall with its foot 6 m from the base of the wall. How far up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse, so $h^2 + 6^2 = 10^2$, giving $h^2 = 100 - 36 = 64$ and $h = 8$ m. The height must be less than the ladder length, which rules out the larger options immediately.

distractorRationale.a: Subtracted the lengths directly instead of their squares
distractorRationale.c: Added the squares, treating the wall height as the hypotenuse
distractorRationale.d: Added the two given lengths
